transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Anna Park (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Velvettech - Head of Security), Evan Li (Velvettech - Platform), Marcos Rivera (Velvettech - CTO)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be noisy): discuss SOC2/ISO gating, ask about BYOK, SSO integration, audit log retention, determine hosting preference, plan benchmark.

[00:00] Anna (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — Anna from Redwood, Samir our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:12] Priya (Velvettech): Hey, thanks. Priya here, and Evan, Marcos — hi.
[00:17] Evan: Hi.
[00:18] Marcos: Good afternoon.
[00:20] Anna: Great. The goal for today is to walk through your security/compliance gates — SOC2, ISO if relevant — how you authenticate users, what kind of RBAC you need, audit logging retention and the key management story. We'll outline Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and capture any blockers. Does that sound right?
[00:35] Marcos: Yep, that's perfect. We're in the middle of a vendor decision — priority is data protection and being able to demonstrate controls to auditors.
[00:42] Priya: Just to add, we have SOC2 in place for core services but product team will need the LLM powered features under the same control plane. We may need ISO27001 too — that's on the roadmap.
[00:51] Samir (Redwood SE): Thanks. Quick question about data classification: do you expect PII/PHI to be sent to the API? Or will you do client-side redaction?
[00:59] Evan: Short answer: some PII is possible — names, emails, occasionally customer notes that include limited PHI. We plan to actively redact, but we need vendor guarantees for logs and retention.
[01:12] Priya: Also need to confirm we can BYOK for encryption keys or use HSM-backed keys; auditors require key separation for certain workflows.
[01:20] Anna: Understood. On Redwood we support hosted with Redwood-managed keys, Dedicated with options for BYOK, and Private where customers retain full control — can run in their VPC/on-prem. BYOK and HSM integration varies by deployment.
[01:33] Evan: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private from an auditor perspective?
[01:36] Samir: Sure. Dedicated is our reserved capacity offering — you get dedicated GPU pools logically isolated for your account, network isolation at the infra layer and storage separation. Logs and metrics still flow to Redwood's control plane but we can apply data partitioning and tighter retention policies. Private is where the control plane can be customer-hosted or a private cloud; you manage networking, and we can offer an air-gapped on-prem package. From an audit standpoint, Private gives you the most direct control to show isolation.
[02:07] Marcos: Ok, good. What about SSO? We use SAML-based SSO with SCIM for provisioning.
[02:14] Anna: We support SSO SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync and group mapping. RBAC can map to your IDP groups.
[02:22] Priya: Are there limits on role granularity? We need 'viewer', 'admin', 'security-auditor' and 'ops' roles and ability to create custom roles.
[02:30] Samir: Yes, role-based access can be customized — you can define fine-grained policies per model, per route. A note — in the hosted product some super-fine bits like per-key token scoping are on roadmap, but for Dedicated and Private you get wider control.
[02:45] Evan: And SCIM is bi-directional? We want deprovisioning to be enforced immediately when someone is removed.
[02:51] Anna: We do just-in-time deprovisioning via SCIM pushes; latencies are typically sub-minute but depends on your IdP. We'll share docs with config examples for Okta/Azure AD.
[03:02] Marcos: Good. Audit logs — for compliance we need immutable logs accessible for 1 year, with export to our SIEM. Can Redwood provide that?
[03:12] Samir: Audit logs capture token to user mapping, requests metadata, response hashes, and admin actions. Hosted: we retain logs by default 90 days, export via S3 or streaming to your SIEM is available as an add-on. Dedicated: retention and export are configurable; Private: full control. For immutability you can ship logs to a write-once S3 bucket or integrate with your log retention policy.
[03:38] Priya: The immutability part is key for auditors. And we need redaction options — e.g., ability to not persist model outputs for certain routes.
[03:46] Samir: We have per-route storage policies: ephemeral-only (no retention), redact-on-ingest (mask PII), and full retention. We can also filter out model outputs before persisting. For hosted customers we can implement redaction hooks; for Dedicated you can run in an architecture where outputs never leave your VPC if you choose Private or Dedicated with strict egress controls.
[04:08] Evan: OK. Encryption — if we do BYOK, what's the flow? Do we rotate keys? Is envelope encryption supported?
[04:16] Anna: Yes — envelope encryption is our standard. You can bring your own key via cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) or via HSM. We support key rotation workflows and can store only encrypted envelopes in our services. For strict separation we'd recommend Private with a customer-managed KMS endpoint.
[04:33] Marcos: Do you support HSM attestation and FIPS modules?
[04:36] Samir: We integrate with cloud HSMs; for FIPS-level requirements we have guidance and customers typically run Private with HSM-backed keys. We'll share our HSM integration notes — some configs require additional contracts.
[04:49] Priya: Audit trail for key usage — we need to show which key decrypts when. Is that logged?
[04:54] Samir: Yes, key usage is logged and can be exported; in Hosted we surface usage metadata, in Dedicated/Private you host logs end-to-end.
[05:05] Anna: Quick question on failover posture. If you choose Dedicated and we have capacity issues, do you want automated fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant or strict fail-close to avoid egress?
[05:16] Marcos: Auditors want strict controls; we prefer no silent fallback that sends data to a shared pool. If fallback is used it must be explicit and recorded.
[05:24] Samir: We can do opt-in fallback policies; default for enterprise is fail-close. We'll document the behavior.
[05:31] Evan: Tokenization — can we tokenize sensitive fields before sending?
[05:35] Samir: Yes, many customers do client-side tokenization and send non-sensitive references. We also support request-level hooks to pre-process payloads.
[05:43] Priya: On data retention, we need different policies by class: PII — 90 days max unless explicitly needed; system logs — 365 days; audit logs — 2+ years in some regs. Can Redwood support differential retention?
[05:58] Anna: Yes, per-route and per-dataset retention policies exist. For Hosted there are constraints but we offer an add-on for extended retention. Dedicated/Private are fully configurable. We'll need to see your classification matrix to map.
[06:12] Evan: We'll send that. What about data residency — can you ensure data stays in region (EU/US)?
[06:18] Samir: We run region-specific clusters; for Hosted we can pin customers to specific regions and for Dedicated/Private it's straightforward. For certain regs we recommend Private in a local region.
[06:28] Marcos: Encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS?
[06:31] Anna: TLS 1.2+ in transit, rest is encrypted with KMS-managed keys or BYOK per deployment. We also support mutual TLS for private endpoints.
[06:40] Priya: Regarding SOC2 artifacts — do you provide controls mapping and evidence packages for auditors?
[06:45] Anna: Yes — we provide a controls matrix, SOC2 report, and a summary of policies. For Dedicated/Private we can provide additional evidence and host cooperative audits.
[06:55] Evan: If we go Dedicated, will the security contact have direct access to raw logs?
[06:59] Samir: Yes, Dedicated customers can opt-in to raw log access — typically via secure S3 buckets or a log streaming endpoint. For Hosted, we provide filtered exports.
[07:10] Marcos: Is there a standard SLA for latency? We need to present numbers to product for decisioning.
[07:15] Samir: Hosted latency profiles are published; Dedicated has predictable throughput with lower p99s since you don't share GPU pools. We'll attach our latency deck and the performance profile table. We'll also run a benchmark on your payloads as agreed.
[07:28] Priya: One more Q on RBAC auditing — we need to be able to prove who accessed which model and when, ideally with a tamper-evident trail.
[07:37] Samir: Audit logs include model access events and admin changes. For tamper-evidence we recommend exporting to append-only storage or integrating with a ledger. We can provide patterns customers use (e.g., write-once S3 + SHA chains).
[07:52] Anna: I'll capture that as an action.
[07:55] [crosstalk] Marcos: — and retention of audit logs for at least 12 months as a minimum.
[07:59] Anna: Noted.
[08:02] Evan: Quick nit — our security team wants to review any third-party subprocessors. Do you maintain a subprocessors list?
[08:10] Anna: Yes we have a subprocessors page; we also provide DPA and subprocessor annex on request. We'll include that link in the binder.
[08:18] Priya: Can you share an example DPA and the redaction SLA?
[08:22] Anna: Yes — we'll include template DPA and the retention/redaction SLAs.
[08:26] Marcos: About cost — Dedicated commitments are a bigger lift. If we prove the cost per 1M tokens versus hosted with caching and batching, we can justify it.
[08:36] Samir: That's exactly the benchmark we'll run — cost-per-token and p99 latency for your payloads with caching bật (sic) and quantization profiles. We'll include recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
[08:50] Evan: Any constraints on model variants for Dedicated? We need a few open models plus a fine-tuned internal model.
[08:57] Samir: Dedicated supports pinned model versions and model rollouts; fine-tuned models are supported, and you can control which versions serve traffic. Private gives the most latitude.
[09:08] Priya: What about pen testing? Do you allow customer-led pentests?
[09:13] Anna: We do — there is an approval process and a scope template. For Dedicated/Private you can run broader tests; for hosted it's limited to non-destructive and agreed-upon windows.
[09:26] Evan: Good. Onboarding timeline — if we decide to pilot in June, what are typical lead times?
[09:30] Samir: Hosted — minutes to hours for API keys. Dedicated — depends on capacity and contract, typically a few weeks to provision. Private — delivery timelines vary widely depending on on-prem environment, often 4-8 weeks. We'll provide a plan.
[09:47] Priya: We may need to show auditors the planned architecture — can you produce a compliance architecture diagram?
[09:52] Anna: Yes, we can provide a compliance-ready architecture diagram showing encryption flows, key custody, and network boundaries. We'll tailor it to Dedicated vs Private.
[10:02] Marcos: Anything else from the team?
[10:05] Evan: Not right now.
[10:06] Priya: No.
[10:07] Anna: OK, recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security binder link, subprocessors list, DPA template, RBAC/audit export patterns, and run the perf/cost benchmark. Samir will lead the benchmark. Priya/Evan will send data classification and sample payloads. Everyone aligned?
[10:23] Priya: Yes.
[10:24] Marcos: Yes.
[10:25] Anna: Great — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for a benchmark review next week. Thanks all.

Meeting end.
